bluf.headline: SAF training infrastructure (SAFTI City, MMRC 2) lands as peer forces surface institutional rather than technological gaps in tech adoption. The window to design SAF training doctrine around these facilities is now.
bluf.summary: Four May 2026 developments frame this bulletin. War on the Rocks documents the US Army's failed decade of manned-unmanned teaming and names the failure modes (culture, talent, feedback) as institutional rather than technological. MMRC 2's two double-height ranges, announced 27 February 2026 and operational by 2031, are purpose-built for manned-unmanned teaming training. The time to write the doctrine, design the curriculum, and reform the operator pathway is now, not in 2031. Project Flytrap 5.0 at Pabradė shows US 2nd Cavalry generating drone-warfare TTPs at squadron level in a temporary range; SAFTI City with its 11,000 sensors is purpose-built to capture and analyse the same kind of exercise. SOCOM at SOF Week disclosed heavy generative-AI use for staff workflows that the SAF Training Analytics branch is now chartered to apply. NGC2's May Ivy Mass red-team event tests the Continuous Transformation acquisition model with direct implications for SAF C2 build-and-train sequencing.

key_developments.title: MMRC 2 announced with MUM-T ranges; Steckler names the institutional failure modes SAF must avoid
key_developments.what: MINDEF announced MMRC 2 on 27 February 2026, operational by 2031, with two double-height ranges purpose-built for manned-unmanned teaming training. In May 2026, Jake Steckler in War on the Rocks documented the US Army's decade-long failed effort to integrate Apaches with Shadow drones and named the failure modes as cultural inertia, talent-model mismatch, and feedback suppression - not hardware.
key_developments.so_what: SAF has roughly five years to write MUM-T training doctrine, draft the operator pathway, and design the curriculum that MMRC 2 will use. The Steckler failure modes are the warning. The right next action is a TDDG cross-branch working group with SAFTI MI and Army CSC to draft the MMRC 2 training-doctrine specification by end FY27, two years before facility delivery.

key_developments.title: Project Flytrap 5.0 is the exercise SAFTI City was instrumented for
key_developments.what: US 2nd Cavalry Regiment ran Project Flytrap 5.0 at Pabradė in Lithuania in May 2026, integrating over 20 pieces of counter-UAS and friendly-UAS equipment at troop and squadron level. The unit developed new TTPs for synchronising intelligence, fires, and maneuver under a multi-layered drone threat.
key_developments.so_what: SAFTI City has 11,000 sensors and the capacity for two concurrent battalion-level exercises. The same mixed-stack drone problem could be instrumented at SAFTI City in ways the US 2nd Cavalry could not. Cap Dev (Sim) and the SAFTI City management team should co-design a SAF Flytrap-equivalent for the next training cycle, with Training Analytics owning the data product.

key_developments.title: SOCOM generative-AI use sets the reference pattern for SAF training-admin AI
key_developments.what: At SOF Week 2026 in Tampa, SOCOM disclosed heavy current use of generative AI for resource allocation and force deployment. The target is smaller models running at the tactical edge under fog-computing architectures, sourced from smaller startups rather than incumbent vendors.
key_developments.so_what: The SAF Training Analytics branch is chartered to apply AI to training admin, safety, and outcomes. SOCOM has done the discovery and named the constraints. SAF can write a 90-day specification for the highest-value workflows (range booking, safety scans, exercise design assistance, outcome summarisation) and pilot one with a willing formation - rather than re-derive the same conclusions over 18-24 months.

key_developments.title: Continuous Transformation acquisition model tested at division scale (Ivy Mass, May 2026)
key_developments.what: The US 4th Infantry Division's May Ivy Mass event puts the next-generation command-and-control (NGC2) prototype against a red team for the first time at division scale. The Continuous Transformation acquisition model has over a dozen vendors building the system while soldiers test it. NGC2 was tested in DDIL conditions in Ivy Sting 4.
key_developments.so_what: The Continuous Transformation model is the transferable lesson for SAF. SAF C2 programmes face the same question: build linearly with risk of obsolescence, or build-while-using with risk of incoherence. Doctrine Development should draft a short note on what concurrent build-and-train means for SAF acquisition doctrine. DDIL should be a configurable parameter at SAFTI City.

branch_sections.summary: May 2026 surfaces three Cap Dev (Sim) opportunities: design a SAFTI City Flytrap-equivalent exercise; embed AI-enabled OPFOR and friendly drone behaviours in simulation systems; and standardise DDIL injection as a configurable simulation parameter. The cross-learning charter for the branch lines up directly with the three reference cases this month.

cross_cutting_themes.theme: SAF training infrastructure landed before peer-force institutional learning caught up - the design window is now
cross_cutting_themes.description: Three articles describe the same gap from different angles: 2nd Cavalry developed drone-warfare TTPs at Pabradė in a temporary range with no native instrumentation; SOCOM is reorganising acquisition around generative-AI patterns that emerged from heavy informal use; the US Army's manned-unmanned teaming effort failed for a decade on cultural and talent-model questions before facilities ever opened. SAFTI City is operational since October 2024 with 11,000 sensors; MMRC 2 is announced with purpose-built MUM-T ranges. The infrastructure is ahead of the doctrine, curriculum, and operator-pathway design needed to use it well. The lesson from peer forces is institutional, and SAF holds the rare advantage of being able to design those institutions before the building opens.
